paragraphs: Military Boots is a pair of laced combat boots with high shafts, padded collars and thick lug soles built for rough ground. The 16,688 polygons go mostly into the eyelets, the stitched seams of the upper and the deep tread pattern underneath. Standing side by side, the pair reads well on a barracks floor, beside a bunk or at the edge of a tent.

A mesh of quads and triangles holds 16,748 vertices, and its UVs are spread without any overlapping islands. The 4 maps at 2048 x 2048 carry the scuffed leather, the darker toe caps and the rubber of the outsole. CheckMate Pro certification means the boots arrive at real scale with clean geometry and materials already assigned.

First offered in 2015, the model has long served war films, soldier characters and military memorial scenes. The laces are tied tight and the tongues sit flat, so the boots look worn by someone rather than shop fresh. At $49 they make a dependable footwear piece for a uniform close up or an equipment flat lay.

This Peltophorum Pterocarpum Tree with Flowers is a mature copperpod with a broad umbrella crown dotted with yellow blossom clusters. Its 3,695,583 polygons are spent on separate leaflets, upright flower spikes and a trunk that forks low above the roots. Planted along a boulevard or beside a tropical resort pool, the tree casts a wide patch of dappled shade.

With 5,353,038 vertices this is a hero asset for close shots rather than a background filler for distant forests. The UV layout keeps every island apart, which makes it easy to swap in your own bark or petal shaders. A CheckMate Lite pass confirms that the file opens cleanly and the branches are modeled at believable scale.

Available since 2021, the copperpod fits landscape plans for hot climates, campus courtyards and Southeast Asian street scenes. Fine feathery foliage lets light through the canopy, so the ground below keeps a soft broken pattern of sun. Priced at $49, it suits architects who need one convincing specimen tree at the center of a garden render.

Prison Cell is a cramped holding room closed off by a front wall of vertical bars and a barred door. Only 17,432 polygons cover the whole interior, since flat walls and a plain floor need little geometry to look right. Shot through the bars from the corridor, the room gives a crime drama an instant sense of confinement.

The 17,715 vertices are unwrapped into separate islands, and 6 maps at 2048 x 2048 add stains and worn paint. That grime on the walls and floor matters, because a spotless cell would read as a set rather than a jail. CheckMate Pro approval guarantees real dimensions, so a character model can stand inside without any rescaling.

The cell has been around since 2015 and still turns up in police shows, game levels and escape room concepts. Repeat it along a corridor and you have a full cell block with very little extra scene weight. For $49 it covers the most common prison interior a story needs, from arrest scenes to visiting days.

This Private Submarine is a compact leisure sub with a rounded hull, a raised conning section and stern propulsion. The budget of 29,544 polygons keeps the smooth hull curvature clean while leaving room for viewports and fins. Underwater, the sub reads best lit from above, gliding past a reef wall or hovering beside a yacht hull.

There are 28,540 vertices here, slightly fewer than faces, which points to a mesh built by hand rather than converted. The UV mapping is mixed, so plan on some extra unwrapping before painting detailed decals or rust onto the shell. It passed the CheckMate Lite review, which covers clean file structure and a hull built at sensible scale.

In circulation since 2015, the vessel is chosen for luxury yacht tenders, ocean exploration films and marine games. A billionaire's toy parked on the deck of a superyacht is exactly the kind of shot it was made for. For $49 the sub is a quick way to give a harbor or seabed scene a story element.

Ski Lift Tower is a steel chairlift pylon with a crossarm at the top carrying sheave wheels for the haul rope. Most of its 57,838 polygons sit in those wheel assemblies, the service ladder and the bolted base flange. Placed in a row up a snowy slope, a few towers turn an empty mountainside into a working ski resort.

The mesh is built entirely from quads, with 62,172 vertices that subdivide cleanly for close inspection shots. Its 5 maps at 4096 x 4096 hold painted metal, rust streaks and the black rubber lining of the sheaves. UVs are laid out without overlaps, and the CheckMate Lite stamp confirms the tower opens at true scale.

On the market since 2018, the pylon serves winter sports games, alpine tourism promos and mountain resort masterplans. Add a cable between two towers and hang chairs from it, and the lift is ready to animate. At $49, a single model covers every tower of the line, since the pylons on a real lift look alike.

Soda Fountain Dispenser is a countertop beverage machine with a row of push levers, nozzles and a drip tray below. The 37,952 polygons concentrate on the valve heads and the rounded edges of the stainless steel housing. Set against a diner wall or a fast food counter, it instantly tells the viewer where the scene takes place.

Behind the shell are 39,177 vertices, unwrapped so that no two islands share texture space. There are 9 maps at 4096 x 4096, enough to keep brushed metal and glossy plastic trim sharp in a close crop. Being CheckMate Pro certified, the dispenser comes at real scale with materials ready for any major renderer.

Available since 2018, the machine is a staple of restaurant interiors, cinema lobbies and convenience store aisles. Paired with a stack of paper cups and an ice bin, it fills the drinks station in a single move. At $49 the unit is priced for interior designers who furnish food courts and quick service chains.

St Edwards Crown with Fur recreates the solid gold coronation crown of the British monarchy, with its ermine band and velvet cap. Four crosses alternate with four fleurs-de-lis around the rim, and two arches meet under a jeweled monde and cross. The fur trim at the base is what separates this version from a bare metal crown on a display stand.

Gemstones set along the arches catch highlights well, so a slow turntable shows off the faceted stones nicely. The crown carries the CheckMate Pro mark, a guarantee of correct scale, tidy topology and working materials. Velvet in the cap and the soft white ermine need different shaders, so each surface is worth tuning on its own.

Released in 2015, the model is picked for coronation reenactments, royal history documentaries and fantasy court scenes. Resting on a red cushion or placed on a seated king, it becomes the focal point of any throne room. At $49, it gives museum displays and period dramas a convincing piece of regalia without building one from scratch.

Stadium Seating Tribune is a stepped spectator stand with rows of molded plastic seats rising on a concrete terrace. Each seat is modeled individually, which is where most of the 542,881 polygons in the stand end up. Viewed from the pitch, the tiers fill the background of a football match, a track meet or an outdoor concert.

With 561,760 vertices the tribune is heavy, so treat it as a hero section and duplicate it with instancing. A set of 25 maps at 4096 x 4096 covers seat plastic, worn concrete steps, railings and stair markings. The non-overlapping UVs and CheckMate Pro certification mean the stand renders correctly straight out of the file.

Since 2019 the stand has filled sports arenas in games, broadcast graphics and architectural studies of new venues. Empty seats suit a quiet training day, while a crowd system can populate them for a packed derby. Priced at $49, it saves days of modeling repetitive rows and lets the work go into the pitch instead.

The United States Weather Satellite GOES-8 3D Model shows a geostationary weather satellite with its solar array and imaging instruments. Its 113,534 polygons describe the boxy bus, the long single solar wing and the solar sail boom balancing it. Shown against the dark limb of the Earth, the spacecraft explains weather forecasting better than any diagram.

The mesh holds 115,544 vertices, all unwrapped into separate islands for clean texture painting. Thermal blankets in gold foil, radiator panels and dark solar cells come from 28 maps at 4096 x 4096. CheckMate Pro certification adds real scale and a tidy hierarchy, which helps when the array needs to rotate.

Published in 2016, the satellite is chosen for meteorology explainers, space agency documentaries and orbital simulation games. Its long asymmetric profile makes for a striking silhouette when the sun sits just behind the spacecraft. For $49 the satellite is a detailed piece of real hardware rather than a generic science fiction probe.

Utility Pole is a tall roadside power pole with crossarms, insulators and the hardware that carries overhead lines. At 157,466 polygons the pole is unusually dense, with bolts, brackets and insulator ribs modeled rather than painted. Lined up along a rural road, a series of these poles gives a landscape scale and a sense of distance.

The 164,124 vertices are fully unwrapped with no overlaps, which leaves room to add weathered wood or concrete textures. No texture maps come with the model, so it suits artists who prefer to build their own materials. CheckMate Pro certification confirms real height, so wires strung between two poles sag at a believable span.

Out since 2023, the pole populates suburban streets, city outskirts and post-storm scenes for film and games. A slight tilt and a few hanging cables are enough to make it read as old neighborhood infrastructure. For $49 it is a reusable street element that architects and environment artists can drop into any town.

Xiaomi Mi Smart Band 4 Fitness Tracker is a slim wristband with a pill-shaped touch display set into a soft silicone strap. The 5,374 polygons go into the curved glass capsule, the strap holes and the round touch button under the screen. Worn on a runner's wrist or lying next to a phone, the band reads clearly even at small sizes.

With 5,477 vertices the tracker stays light enough to place on an animated character without slowing the viewport. Its UVs are unwrapped cleanly with no overlaps, ready for a custom watch face or a different strap color. The model holds CheckMate Pro status, so it arrives at real wrist scale with tidy, well named parts.

On offer since 2020, it appears in fitness app mockups, tech review videos and gym lifestyle scenes. Branded hardware like this falls under editorial use, which fits news pieces, reviews and educational material. At $49 the band adds a recognizable real gadget to any close shot of a wrist or a desk.

Xray Brain Hologram is a glowing see-through brain with both hemispheres, the cerebellum and the brain stem in translucent form. Its 42,122 polygons trace the folds of the cortex closely, which matters once light passes through the surface. Floating above a lab desk or a medical interface, the hologram signals neuroscience at a glance.

The 21,063 vertices are half the face count, typical of a fully triangulated surface. No maps are included, since the look depends on a glowing, transparent shader rather than on painted textures. UVs are still laid out without overlaps, and CheckMate Pro approval confirms the brain is modeled at real scale.

First available in 2024, the hologram fits sci-fi hospitals, neurology lectures and medical technology explainers. Animated with a slow spin and a scan line passing through it, the brain becomes an instant futuristic diagnostic display. For $49 it works equally well in a game HUD, a film interface or a conference presentation.

iPad Air 2 Silver and Smart Case pairs the thin aluminum tablet with the folding magnetic cover Apple made for it. The silver back, the rounded edges and the round home button below the screen are all reproduced faithfully. Folded into a triangle, the cover props the tablet up on a desk for typing or watching video.

The model is built to CheckMate specification, which means correct proportions and a clean, organized scene file. The segmented panels of the cover make the folding mechanism easy to read even from a distance. A glossy black screen gives you a ready surface for placing any interface image or wallpaper.

On the market since 2015, the tablet suits office scenes, classrooms and home interiors from the middle of that decade. As a branded Apple device it carries an editorial license, suited to journalism, tutorials and product reviews. At $44 it is a quick way to put a recognizable tablet on a desk or in a character's hands.

Manger With Swaddling Cloth is a rustic wooden feeding trough filled with straw and lined with a draped linen cloth. A large share of the 376,263 polygons goes into the individual straw stalks and the soft folds of the fabric. Set inside a stable with a lantern glow, it becomes the quiet center of a Nativity scene.

The vertex count of 632,139 runs well above the faces, a sign of dense, finely split geometry in the straw. Being a StemCell model, it renders consistently across several major engines with matching materials. There are no texture maps, but the UVs are laid without overlaps so wood grain can be added easily.

Offered since 2022, the manger is picked for Christmas cards, church pageant visuals and holiday animation. Lit from above by a single warm source, the cloth catches the light and draws the eye to the cradle. Priced at $44, it frees artists from building straw by hand for a seasonal project.

Cricket Generic Collection gathers unbranded cricket gear into one set, ready to dress a pitch, a pavilion or a locker room. Without logos on the equipment, the pieces fit any team, any league and any period drama without clearance trouble. Typical cricket gear has strong shapes, such as the flat willow bat face and the raised seam of the ball.

Every piece in the collection meets the CheckMate Pro standard for real scale, clean topology and tidy naming. Getting the items together keeps materials consistent, so the gear looks like it belongs to one club. Leather, willow and padded fabric each read differently under stadium floodlights, which helps a close shot.

Available since 2015, the set serves sports games, cricket broadcasts and coaching materials across the Commonwealth. Scatter the pieces on the grass after a match and the scene tells its own story about the game. At $42 the collection costs less than modeling even one of the items properly from reference.

Anodized Industrial Joints Set is a kit of colored aluminum connectors used to join profile beams into frames and machine guards. Across 99,455 polygons, every bracket keeps its slots, bolt holes and chamfered edges crisp and readable. Assembled into a frame, the joints help a factory cell or a laboratory rig look properly engineered.

The 99,515 vertices almost match the face count, which suggests a clean mesh without stray triangles. A generous 21 maps at 2048 x 2048 capture the satin sheen and tinted color of anodized metal. Clean, non-overlapping UVs and a CheckMate Pro badge make the parts dependable for technical renders.

In the range since 2016, the set is used for automation layouts, engineering manuals and workshop interiors. Mixing a few colors along one frame shows off the anodizing better than a uniform gray structure would. At $39 the kit spares engineers from modeling small fittings that eat hours but rarely get noticed in a shot.

Apple EarPods with Remote and Mic Set models the white wired earphones with their in-line remote and the thin cable that joins them. The 43,852 polygons shape the distinctive angled earbuds, the speaker grilles and the volume buttons on the remote. Coiled on a desk or hanging around a character's neck, the earphones add a familiar everyday detail.

Under the glossy white plastic sit 44,350 vertices with UVs unwrapped into non-overlapping islands. There are 11 maps at 2048 x 2048 and 1024 x 1024, covering plastic, metal mesh and the rubbery cable. The CheckMate Pro mark guarantees that the earbuds come at real size and open without missing materials.

Around since 2015, the set lands in commuter scenes, music studio desks and tech journalism illustrations. Being an Apple product, the model is licensed for editorial uses only, such as reviews and news coverage. For $39 you get the earphones at a level of detail that survives a macro shot of the remote.

Automated Warehouse Robot Generic is a low square drive unit that slides under shelving pods and carries them to picking stations. Only 13,386 polygons are needed for the flat body, the lifting turntable on top and the small sensor windows. Dozens of these units moving across a gridded floor make an e-commerce fulfillment center look alive.

Its 13,926 vertices keep the model light enough for crowds of robots in a game or simulation. The 7 maps at 4096 x 4096 give the painted shell, rubber bumpers and status lights plenty of resolution. UV islands never overlap, and the CheckMate Pro rating confirms correct scale for factory layouts.

Since 2020 the robot has stood in for logistics automation in explainer videos, warehouse planning and industry trade show material. Without any brand marks it can represent any operator, which keeps a presentation neutral. For $39 the unit is an easy building block for a full fleet animation across a storage floor.

Baby Plastic Animal Toys is a small group of chunky molded figures with rounded shapes made for little hands. Just 6,336 polygons cover the set, because smooth toy forms need no sharp detail to look convincing. Scattered on a play mat or a nursery rug, the animals instantly suggest a toddler's room.

The 6,351 vertices are unwrapped without overlaps, which keeps the bright plastic colors clean on every figure. A total of 6 maps at 4096 x 4096 give the plastic a soft gloss that holds up in a close family shot. The toys are built to CheckMate specification, so scale and file organization meet a dependable standard.

Offered since 2019, the set appears in baby product scenes, parenting blogs and children's room interiors. Their simple silhouettes stay readable even when the camera pulls back to show a whole living room. At $39 the set gives a family scene its clutter of toys without hours spent on modeling.

Bamboo Grove is a dense clump of tall segmented bamboo stems with narrow leaves fanning out near the top. Its 1,396,658 polygons are mostly foliage, with every leaf blade modeled so the canopy has real depth. Planted beside a temple path or a modern courtyard, the grove adds height and a calm Asian mood.

With 2,009,654 vertices the grove is a heavy close-range asset, best kept for hero shots rather than far backgrounds. UV mapping is mixed, while the 10 maps at 2048 x 2048 handle the green culms, joints and leaf surfaces. CheckMate Pro status confirms that the stems stand at believable height and the scene opens neatly organized.

Since 2019 the grove has served Japanese gardens, spa resorts and tropical jungle sets in games and film. Wind animation suits it well, because the slender stems sway in a way that sells a breezy afternoon. At $39 the grove is a ready screen of greenery that hides fences and frames a garden view.

Bikini Set is a two-piece swimsuit, a top and matching bottoms shaped to fit a female figure. The 8,302 polygons follow the curves of the cups and the thin straps without wasting geometry on flat fabric. Laid on a beach towel or hung on a cabin hook, the swimsuit sets a summer holiday mood.

There are slightly fewer vertices than faces, 8,252 in all, a hint of a closed, carefully built garment mesh. Its 4 maps at 4096 x 4096 carry the fabric color and stitching, sharp enough for a fashion close-up. Non-overlapping UVs make recoloring simple, and the CheckMate Pro rating covers scale and clean topology.

Released in 2015, the swimsuit is used for swimwear catalogs, beach resort scenes and character dressing in games. A simple pattern or a bold print changes the look completely, since the UVs give a clean canvas. At $39 it suits anyone who needs swimwear on a figure without tailoring cloth from scratch.

Bouldering Wall is an indoor climbing panel with angled faces covered in colorful resin holds of many shapes and sizes. The 375,282 polygons go mainly into those holds, each one modeled with its own grip edges and bolt recess. Set behind thick crash mats, the wall turns an empty hall into a busy climbing gym.

Only 176,911 vertices sit under those faces, a ratio that comes from a heavily triangulated surface. No texture maps are supplied, so color the holds to match a real gym or a team identity. Clean UVs without overlaps and CheckMate Pro approval make that recoloring job straightforward and safe.

Available since 2023, the wall appears in fitness center designs, sports campaigns and climbing training content. Route setters love strong color coding, and the varied holds make any marked route easy to read on camera. At $39 the panel is a fast start for a gym interior that would take days to model.

Cabbage Collection brings together several heads of cabbage, with tightly packed leaves and the broad outer wrappers curling back. Prominent veins run across each leaf, and they catch side light in a way that makes the vegetables look freshly picked. Stacked in a market crate or laid on a kitchen board, the heads give a scene an instant farm-fresh feel.

Every model in the set holds the CheckMate Pro rating, which covers real size, clean geometry and working materials. Variety matters with produce, and several different heads avoid the cloned look of one vegetable copied many times. The pale green inner leaves and the darker outer layers give enough contrast for both close and wide shots.

First offered in 2017, the collection serves grocery store aisles, cooking shows and farm scenes in games. A few heads beside a knife and a chopping board are enough to set up a recipe video. At $39 the set covers a whole vegetable stall corner without anyone having to sculpt leaves.

Calophyllum Antillanum is a West Indian laurel tree with a rounded evergreen crown of thick, glossy oval leaves. The 2,453,741 polygons build out each leaf and the branching structure inside the crown, so it holds up at close range. Often planted along coastal streets in Florida, the tree fits waterfront parks and hotel driveways.

Behind that foliage are 2,951,311 vertices, so render it as a featured specimen rather than mass scattering. A large set of 28 maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048 covers bark, leaf tops and the paler undersides. UVs never overlap, and CheckMate Pro certification confirms true height and a well organized scene.

From 2019 onward the laurel has shaded Caribbean resort plans, coastal promenades and tropical game levels. Its dense, dark canopy throws deep shade, which helps a sunny plaza feel cooler and more inviting. For $39 the tree delivers botanical accuracy that generic tropical foliage packs rarely match.

Castle Entrance with Clock is a stone gatehouse with an arched passage, battlements on top and a large clock face above the gate. Its 145,392 polygons carve out individual blocks, the deep arch and the numerals and hands of the clock. Seen from a cobbled square, the gate gives an old town or a fairy tale kingdom its main landmark.

The 145,493 vertices match the faces almost exactly, a sign of a clean shell with few stray edges. Weathered masonry, dark weathering in the joints and the painted dial come from 14 maps at 4096 x 4096. With non-overlapping UVs and the CheckMate Pro mark, the gatehouse is ready to render without cleanup.

Out since 2019, it serves medieval games, historical documentaries and theme park concept art. The clock gives the scene a storytelling device, a reminder that something happens at a set hour. At $39 the entrance is a strong anchor for a walled city built from smaller modular pieces.

Concert Stage Array Audio System is a hanging line array of stacked speaker cabinets, rigged from a frame above the stage. Its 56,632 polygons describe the curved column of boxes, the grilles on their fronts and the flying hardware between them. Hung on both sides of a festival stage, the arrays frame the band and make the venue feel large.

The 59,300 vertices are unwrapped into tidy, non-overlapping islands across every cabinet. Only 3 maps at 1204 x 1024 cover the black finish, so the system is meant to be seen from a distance. A CheckMate Pro badge confirms real cabinet sizes, which helps when the rig has to match a stage plan.

On offer since 2018, the array fills rock concerts, music festivals and event production previews. Event planners use rigs like this to show a client where sound will hang before a show is built. Priced at $39, it is a simple way to give a stage design proper professional audio.

Concrete Drainage Pipes Set is a group of heavy precast pipe sections of the kind stacked at road and sewer construction sites. Thick walls and flared socket ends show how the segments slot together once they are laid in a trench. Piled beside a dug-up street or rolled into a field, the pipes tell the viewer that work is underway.

Each section follows the CheckMate specification, so pieces arrive at true scale with a clean scene hierarchy. Rough gray concrete with a slightly pitted surface reads well under harsh midday light on a building site. Children's games and urban exploration scenes also use large pipes as hiding spots and tunnels.

Around since 2015, the pipes populate civil engineering presentations, infrastructure videos and construction levels in games. Stacked in a pyramid with timber wedges, they make a convincing storage yard at a precast plant. For $39 the set saves time on a prop that every road works scene seems to need.

Cooler Master Hyper 212 RGB Black Edition CPU Cooler is a tower air cooler with a black fin stack and a lit fan. Its 238,267 polygons separate every aluminum fin, the heat pipes and the blades of the RGB fan. Mounted on a motherboard inside a glass-sided case, the cooler becomes the visual centerpiece of a gaming build.

The 235,711 vertices sit on a mesh that is clean enough to hold every fin edge in a macro shot. As a StemCell model it renders the same way in different engines, with 6 maps at 2048 x 2048 for metal and plastic. UV islands are laid flat without overlap, so the brushed fin finish can be adjusted without stretching.

Out since 2020, the cooler shows up in PC building guides, hardware reviews and tech channel thumbnails. Being a trademarked product, it is licensed for editorial use, which suits explainers and press coverage. For $39 it gives a computer interior the familiar tower cooler that enthusiasts expect to see.

Coxed Four Boat 3D Model is a narrow racing shell for four rowers and a coxswain, with sliding seats and long sweep oars. The 84,221 polygons shape the thin hull, the riggers, the foot stretchers and the blade ends of the oars. Gliding across a calm lake at dawn, the boat sets up the classic image of a rowing regatta.

There are 87,262 vertices under a surface clean enough to show reflections running along the glossy hull. The hull and rigging draw on 5 maps at 4096 x 4096, with UVs kept free of any overlap. StemCell certification means the boat looks consistent whether it is rendered in V-Ray, Arnold or a game engine.

Available from 2019, the shell suits Olympic sports graphics, university rowing club visuals and sports simulations. Add rower figures on the seats and a cox at the stern, and the crew is ready to race. At $39 the boat is far cheaper than modeling a fragile racing hull and its rigging by hand.

Digital Pixel Pattern Soccer Ball(1) is a match ball wrapped in a blocky pixel graphic instead of the classic pentagon panels. The square pixel blocks give the ball a retro video game look that stands out on a green pitch. Spinning in flight, the pattern blurs into bright streaks that read well in slow-motion shots.

The ball meets the CheckMate Pro standard, which guarantees real scale, smooth topology and assigned materials. A round shape is unforgiving, so clean geometry matters for reflections across the glossy outer skin. Seams between panels are subtle, letting the printed design carry most of the visual interest.

Released in 2023, the ball works for football game assets, sports brand concepts and esports themed graphics. Placed on a penalty spot or resting at the foot of a player, it gives a familiar object a fresh twist. For $39 the ball is a quick prop that connects football with gaming culture in one image.

Firefighting Coat is a heavy turnout jacket with reflective bands, a high storm collar and wide cuffs for working in heat. Only 4,918 polygons form the jacket, with the folds of thick fabric built into the shape rather than sculpted in detail. Hung on a hook in a fire station locker, the coat sets the scene before a single truck appears.

Its 4,983 vertices keep the coat light, so it can sit on a crowd of rescue characters in real time. No textures come with it, but the non-overlapping UVs are ready for tan fabric, soot and reflective trim. The CheckMate Lite review checked that the file opens cleanly and the jacket is built at human scale.

In the range since 2021, the coat equips firefighter characters, fire safety training and emergency service dramas. A touch of soot on the shoulders and sleeves quickly turns a clean garment into one that has seen a blaze. At $39 it is an affordable piece of protective gear for any rescue or disaster scene.

Florida Royal Palm Roystonea Regia is a tall palm with a smooth gray trunk, a green crownshaft and arching feathery fronds. The 355,513 polygons split each frond into individual leaflets, so the crown looks full from any angle. Lined along a boulevard or a hotel entrance, royal palms give a Florida setting its unmistakable vertical rhythm.

With 553,977 vertices the palm sits between light filler and hero asset, fine for mid-distance avenues. There are 15 maps at 4800 x 3000 and 4096 x 4096 for bark, the crownshaft and both sides of the fronds. Unwrapped without overlaps and certified CheckMate Pro, the palm opens at true height with materials in place.

Since 2019 the palm has lined Miami streets, Caribbean resorts and tropical real estate renders. Its clean, column-like trunk catches low sun beautifully and throws long shadows across a plaza. For $39 the palm is a dependable choice for landscape architects working on warm coastal projects.

Fortune Cookies in Bowl is a small dish piled with folded golden cookies, each bent into the familiar crescent shape. With 7,700 polygons the scene stays light, while the creased edges of each cookie remain crisp and believable. Placed at the end of a Chinese restaurant meal, the bowl closes the table scene with a playful touch.

The 7,720 vertices are mapped without overlaps, and 11 maps at 4096 x 4096 give the baked surface its toasty color. Tiny surface bumps and darker edges come through in close food photography without extra modeling. StemCell certification makes the cookies look the same across the major renderers, which matters for food scenes.

Offered since 2020, the bowl suits Asian restaurant interiors, Lunar New Year visuals and food blog illustrations. Next to a pot of tea and chopsticks, the bowl reads as dessert at a family dinner. At $39 it is a charming small prop that adds cultural detail to a dining scene.

Garage Tool Rack is a wall-mounted metal rack holding a full spread of hand tools on hooks and shelves. Most of the 213,223 polygons go into the tools themselves, so each grip and jaw reads clearly up close. Fixed above a workbench, the rack instantly turns an empty wall into a working home garage.

The 213,786 vertices nearly equal the faces, a sign of tidy modeling across dozens of small parts. No texture maps are included, so the steel, rubber and painted metal are left for you to shade. Non-overlapping UVs and the CheckMate Pro seal make that material work quick and predictable for any artist.

Since 2021 the rack has furnished DIY tutorials, hardware store visuals and garage renovation renders. A slightly cluttered arrangement suggests real use, which suits stories set in a family workshop. At $39 the rack saves the long job of modeling every tool for a single background wall.

Heavy Duty Rack Flight Case with Wheels 52x48x48cm is a road case with aluminum edges, steel corners and recessed handles. The 435,924 polygons capture rivets, latches and the caster wheels, so the case survives a close inspection. Rolled to the side of a stage or stacked in a tour truck, it signals touring life immediately.

With 223,869 vertices, roughly half the face count, the mesh is largely triangulated around its hardware. There are no textures, so the black laminate panels and metal trim are yours to shade. Clean UVs without overlaps keep that process simple, and CheckMate Pro approval keeps the scale correct.

Released in 2023, the case suits concert backstage scenes, music equipment rental visuals and touring documentaries. Covered with stickers and scuffs, it looks like gear that has crossed a few continents with a band. For $39 the case is a strong supporting prop for any stage crew or rehearsal room shot.

HTC Vive XR Elite with Controllers shows the compact mixed reality headset alongside its two tracked handheld controllers. The 96,648 polygons go into the goggle-like front visor, the rear battery strap and the ring-free controller shells. Resting on a desk or worn by a character, the headset signals virtual reality without any explanation.

Only 50,669 vertices hold those faces, which means a fairly triangulated mesh around the curved shells. No textures are supplied, yet the non-overlapping UVs are ready for matte plastic and glossy lens materials. Its StemCell status ensures the device looks consistent across the renderers that TurboSquid supports for its certified models.

Out since 2024, the set appears in tech reviews, VR arcade interiors and XR training explainers. As trademarked hardware, the model carries an editorial license meant for news, education and honest product reviews. At $39 it puts a current headset into a gaming room or office scene with very little effort.

Human Small Intestines is an anatomical model of the coiled small bowel, the long folded tube packed into the abdomen. An efficient 8,080 polygons trace the overlapping loops of the bowel, keeping the organ smooth without becoming heavy. Placed inside a transparent torso, the coils show students where digestion and absorption take place.

The 8,082 vertices are unwrapped cleanly with no overlapping islands, which suits detailed medical texturing. Its 5 maps at 4096 x 4096 and 2048 x 2048 give the moist pink tissue and fine blood vessels. CheckMate Pro approval confirms anatomical scale, so the organ sits correctly inside a full body model.
